classification.difficultyReason: Build the three-stage tree and distinguish exactly one head from at least one head when selecting favourable paths.

content.prompt: A coin is tossed three times.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a tree diagram showing all the outcomes.

answer.short: The tree has outcomes $HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH, TTT$.
answer.worked: At each of three stages, branch into $H$ and $T$. There are $2\times2\times2=8$ paths, one for each ordered outcome.

spec.description: Three-stage binary tree with H above T at every split and all eight terminal outcomes labelled.
spec.mathematics: All ordered sequences of three H/T results.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the probability that three heads are obtained?

answer.worked:
Only $HHH$ gives three heads, out of eight equally likely paths.
$$P(\text{three heads})=\frac18$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is the probability that exactly one head is obtained?

answer.worked:
The favourable paths are $HTT, THT, TTH$, out of eight equally likely paths.
$$P(\text{exactly one head})=\frac38$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: What is the probability that at least one head is obtained?

answer.worked:
The favourable paths are $HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH$. Seven of the eight equally likely paths contain a head.
$$P(\text{at least one head})=\frac78$$
